headline: Chips Drag, Defensives Lead as Monday Session Ends in a Narrow Split
body_html:
Monday's session closed on a razor-thin edge, with 276 stocks finishing higher against 261 that fell across the 544-name universe — a market that refused to commit in either direction. The dominant story was a sharp divergence between defensive sectors and technology hardware. Healthcare added 0.59% and Energy gained 0.55%, while Consumer names rose 0.45%, suggesting investors leaned toward resilience over risk as geopolitical headlines out of Saudi Arabia unsettled sentiment.

The semiconductor complex bore the session's heaviest damage, sliding 3.22% as a group — the worst showing of any sector Monday. Homebuilders followed with a 1.44% retreat. Semtech shed 10.15%, Ciena dropped 9.95%, Ichor Holdings fell 9.23%, and Coherent lost 7.87%, leaving networking and chip-equipment names among the day's most bruised corners. Software finished essentially flat, down just a fraction, while Industrials and Materials also dipped modestly into the red.

On the upside, Fair Isaac surged 10.85% to claim the session's top spot, with Victoria's Secret and Manhattan Associates adding 6.90% and 6.34% respectively. As Tuesday approaches, traders will be watching whether semiconductor weakness deepens or stabilizes — because Monday offered no clean answer.

briefs.headline: Fair Isaac Rockets to Session's Top Spot
briefs.body: Fair Isaac shares jumped 10.85% Monday, the strongest single-stock move in the universe for the session. The financial-data firm offered no immediate public catalyst, but the magnitude of the move drew attention across the financial-data sector. Traders will be watching for any after-hours commentary that explains the surge.

briefs.headline: Riyadh Airport Attacks Ripple Through Aviation and Energy Markets
briefs.body: Missile and drone strikes on Saudi Arabian airports this week prompted airlines to cancel services into Riyadh and forced Delta to postpone its planned Atlanta-Riyadh route. The disruptions underscore the fragility of Saudi Arabia's ambitious economic diversification push, with analysts noting that sustained airport closures could weigh on the kingdom's drive to build a global tourism and logistics hub.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Posts Session's Steepest Decline
briefs.body: The semiconductor group fell 3.22% Monday, the hardest-hit sector of the day. Semtech led individual decliners with a 10.15% drop, while Ichor Holdings lost 9.23% and MaxLinear shed 7.46%. The cluster of losses across analog chips, semiconductor equipment, and broader chip names points to sector-specific pressure rather than isolated stock events.

briefs.headline: US-Russia Diesel Deal Stirs Diplomatic Debate
briefs.body: Washington is pursuing a diesel-supply arrangement with Moscow as leverage to soften Russian positions in ongoing peace negotiations, according to sourced reporting. The deal drew pushback from legislators on both sides of the aisle, even as the administration defended the terms. Energy markets are monitoring whether the arrangement reshapes near-term crude and refined-product flows.

briefs.headline: Salesforce Earns a Double Upgrade as 'SaaS Is Dead' Narrative Fades
briefs.body: One Wall Street firm moved Salesforce two full rating notches higher Monday, citing evidence that dire predictions about enterprise software's demise were overblown. The upgrade reflects a broader reassessment of cloud-software fundamentals, even as the Software sector in Monday's session barely budged, finishing down just a fraction of a percent.

briefs.headline: Victoria's Secret and Shopify Pace Consumer and E-Commerce Gains
briefs.body: Victoria's Secret climbed 6.90% Monday, the second-best gain in the universe, while Shopify added 4.90% to round out the top six movers. The paired advances suggest selective appetite for consumer-facing and e-commerce names even as the broader Consumer sector's 0.45% gain remained modest, with investors appearing to favor specific stories over the group wholesale.
